background_notes.fact: For Q=K⊗ℤM with its first-factor K-action, pure tensors span Q as a K-vector space. Consequently two K-linear maps Q→Q agreeing on all a⊗u are equal.

background_notes.justification: The tensor product is generated additively by elementary tensors: its construction is a quotient of the free abelian group on pairs. Thus every element is a finite sum of pure tensors (integer multiples can be absorbed into a factor). Such a sum is also a K-linear combination, and a⊗u=a(1⊗u). Linearity extends agreement on these generators to each finite sum, yielding equality of endomorphisms for every f.

background_notes.fact: In End_K(Q), integer scalar multiplication is multiplication by the corresponding integer image in K. For K-linear endomorphisms T,S and a,b∈K, (aT)∘(bS)=ab(T∘S), and scalar multiplication distributes over finite sums of endomorphisms.

background_notes.justification: Repeated addition and additive inverses on a K-vector space agree with multiplication by the canonical integer image in K. Equivalently the tensor balancing relation gives a⊗zu=(za)⊗u. Evaluating compositions at q∈Q gives aT(bS(q))=abT(S(q)) by K-linearity, while finite distributivity follows pointwise from vector addition. These identities justify both the scalar interpretation after applying Fext and the d⁻¹ normalization calculation.
